post.description:
Ingest a custom event by name.

**Secret API key (`be_…`)** — the event must already be defined for the organization (otherwise 404), and a payload that fails the declared schema is rejected with 422. Identify the contact with at least one of `external_id`, `email` or `phone_number` (several allowed), or with `contact_id` on its own; `contact_id` may not be combined with the others. `anonymous_id` is rejected — a server cannot assert a device-minted id.

**Client key (`pub_…`, from a browser or mobile SDK)** — an unknown event name defines itself, and a schema mismatch is recorded on the event rather than refused, because a shipped client cannot be redeployed to fix a rejection. Identify with at least one of `anonymous_id`, `external_id`, `email` or `phone_number`; `contact_id` is not accepted. Requests carrying an `Origin` header must come from an origin on the organization allowlist.

Identifiers are ranked `contact_id` > `external_id` > `email` > `phone_number` > `anonymous_id`. The highest-ranked match wins; a matched contact adopts any identifier it does not already hold; a lower-ranked contact is merged in only when nothing stronger identifies it, and an ambiguous match is logged rather than merged. `phone_number` must be E.164 (e.g. +966501234567). An unmatched identifier auto-creates a contact.

**Batch** — send `{ "events": [ <item>, ... ] }` (max 50 items, same item shape) instead of a single event. Items are processed independently: a per-item validation error yields `{ "error": ... }` in that item's slot of the `results` array and does not fail the batch. The `Idempotency-Key` header applies to the whole request.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional key (max 256 chars) to make this send idempotent for 24h. Any unique string; a common pattern is <event-type>/<entity-id>.

requestBody.description: A single event, or a batch envelope { "events": [ <same item shape>, ... ] } with up to 50 items.

202.description: Event accepted for processing. A batch returns one result per item.

400.description: No identifier supplied (CONTACT_REQUIRED); contact_id combined with external_id/email/phone_number (CONTACT_AMBIGUOUS); anonymous_id sent with a secret key (ANONYMOUS_ID_NOT_ALLOWED); or contact_id sent with a client key (CONTACT_ID_NOT_ALLOWED)

403.description: Client key used from an origin that is not on the organization allowlist

404.description: Event name not defined for this organization, or contact_id not found. Client keys auto-create the event definition instead

409.description: Idempotency-Key reused with a different payload

422.description: Schema mismatch. Secret keys only — a client key records the errors on the event and accepts it

429.description: Organization's event ingestion budget for the current 60-second window is exhausted. Counted in events, so a batch spends one per item. Retry after the retry-after header

post.description:
The migration path. Same item shape and the same `(organization, installation_id)` upsert as `POST /v1/push/devices`, processed asynchronously.

**Shape errors come back now, everything else is queued.** A row that fails validation is reported inline in `errors` and is never enqueued. The rest are accepted and processed in the background, so a large import is never bounded by a request timeout.

**Contacts are resolved by the full identifier ladder** — `external_id`, then `email`, then `phone_number` — so an export keyed on your own user id works directly, and duplicate contacts consolidate instead of forking. A row whose identifiers match more than one irreconcilable contact is reported rather than guessed at.

**An import never creates a contact.** Import contacts first, then devices, then apply opt-outs with `POST /v1/push/devices/unregister`.

**Poll `GET /v1/push/imports/{id}`** for status, counts and the per-row failures in `errors`.

Rate-limited separately from the rest of the API: 120 calls per minute.

422.description: The envelope itself is invalid — empty, or over the item cap

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Retry after the `retry-after` header.

get.description: `queued` and `processing` mean keep polling. `completed` means every accepted row was attempted — a non-zero `failed` is normal and the reasons are in `errors`, one entry per failed row carrying the `index` it held in your submitted array. `failed` means the job itself died, which is not the same as its rows failing.

post.description:
Durable opt-out recorded as `contact_opt_out`. A later `POST /v1/push/devices` for the same `installation_id` will NOT resurrect it — registration runs on every app launch, so a revocation those calls could undo would be no opt-out at all.

A reinstall is a different case: it mints a new `installation_id` and registers as a new device. What carries the opt-out across a reinstall is the contact-level push consent — revoking a contact's last active device also marks the contact unsubscribed from push, and that is never reversed automatically. The exception is a contact who still holds another active device: there the reinstalled handset becomes reachable again, and you should call this endpoint again if it must stay off.

Modelled as POST rather than DELETE because the installation id travels in the body and DELETE bodies are dropped by a fair number of HTTP clients and proxies.

Addresses a contact, never a device token: an anonymous registration is stored but is not addressable. Every ACTIVE device the contact has registered receives the notification.

Push has no transactional exemption. Unlike email and SMS, there is no statutory carve-out to invoke: consent is a single explicit OS-level grant, the OS enforces it whatever a sender labels the message, and Apple 4.5.4 makes marketing the category that needs extra opt-in. A contact who has opted out of push is refused — send essential service messages over email or SMS instead.

A contact with no active device is a successful skip, not an error: the 202 means accepted for processing, and per-device outcomes land in push analytics.

post.description:
Send a one-off WhatsApp message from an approved template — an OTP, an order update, a receipt.

**Templates are required.** WhatsApp does not allow business-initiated free-text messages. Create a template, wait for Meta to approve it, then send it by name.

**Categories behave differently:**
- `AUTHENTICATION` — pass the one-time code as `parameters.code`. The code is repeated automatically into the copy-code button when the template has one.
- `UTILITY` / `MARKETING` — pass one entry per `{{placeholder}}` in the template body, keyed by placeholder name.

**Delivery is asynchronous.** A 202 means the provider accepted the message, not that it was delivered. Poll `GET /whatsapp/{id}` for the delivery state, which updates as the provider reports it.

**Billing:** charged per message at the rate for the destination country and category, held on acceptance and settled from the delivery receipt. A message the provider rejects is not charged.

post.description:
Create a template and submit it to Meta for review in one call. WhatsApp only lets a business start a conversation with an approved template.

**Approval is asynchronous.** The template comes back `pending`. Poll `GET /whatsapp/templates/{id}` until `status` is `approved` or `rejected`; review usually takes minutes and can take up to 48 hours.

**Marketing and utility** templates carry `components`, in Meta's own format. Headers are text only for now. Placeholders are named in lowercase snake_case (`{{first_name}}`), and those names are the keys you pass in `parameters` when sending.

**Authentication** templates carry `authentication` options instead: Meta fixes the wording, and the one-time code is sent as `parameters.code`.

**Sending:** utility and authentication templates go out through `POST /whatsapp/send`. A marketing template can be created here but is sent as a campaign.

**Retries:** name and language identify a template. Repeating a create that already succeeded returns 409; read it back with `GET /whatsapp/templates?name=`.

Rename it, replace its steps, enable or disable it. In one request these apply in that order: rename, disable, replace the steps, enable. A refused request changes nothing. To change a live automation, send `status: disabled` with the new steps, then `status: enabled`.

Enabling publishes the latest steps, so contacts follow what `get` shows, and starts letting in every contact who matches the trigger: it sends messages. It is refused while `issues` is not empty. Contacts already in the automation keep following the version they entered.

Each contact that enters uses one of the plan’s monthly automation runs. Once they are used up, new entries are skipped until the next period; the automation stays enabled and contacts already in it finish.

The steps of an enabled automation cannot be replaced; disable it first or in the same request.

info.title: Arsel Developer API
info.description:
Developer API for programmatic access to Arsel.

## Authentication
All endpoints require an API key in the Authorization header:
```
Authorization: Bearer be_your_api_key_here
```

Generate API keys from your organization settings in the dashboard.

## Rate Limits
- **1000 requests per minute** per organization
- Rate limit headers included in every response:
  - `ratelimit-limit`: Maximum requests per window
  - `ratelimit-remaining`: Requests remaining
  - `ratelimit-reset`: Seconds until window resets
- HTTP 429 returned when limit exceeded, with `retry-after` header

## Response Format
- **202 Accepted**: Request queued successfully, returns message ID
- **401 Unauthorized**: Invalid or missing API key
- **422 Unprocessable Entity**: Validation error
- **429 Too Many Requests**: Rate limit exceeded

apns_environment.description: Which APNs host this token is addressable on. iOS only. Send `sandbox` for debug and simulator builds — a token minted by one host is rejected by the other, and Apple gives no way to tell them apart from the token. Defaults to `production`, which is what App Store and TestFlight builds mint.

device_token.description: Push token for the device. An FCM registration token on android; the APNs device token on ios.

endpoint.description: Web Push endpoint URL. Required for web.

p256dh_key.description: Web Push P-256 ECDH public key.

enablement_status.description: OS notification permission as your app last observed it. Registration is not consent — a device registers before the prompt and after a denial — so omit this rather than guessing. `provisional` is the iOS mode that delivers quietly to Notification Centre.

sdk_version.description: Arsel SDK build running on the device, e.g. `android/1.2.0`. Supply it only if the SDK is embedded: it is what marks the device as instrumented for delivery/engagements.

device_timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. `Asia/Riyadh`. Unbackfillable — send it.

devices.description: Up to 1000 device registrations, each the single-device body.

index.description: Position of the failed row in the `devices` array you submitted.

message.example: No contact in this organization matches the supplied reference.

rejected.description: Rows rejected on shape and never queued.

errors.description: The rejected rows. Failures that only surface during processing are not here — read the import errors route once the job completes.

status.description: `failed` means the job died, not that its rows did — that is `completed` with a non-zero `failed` count.

errors.description: One entry per failed row, each carrying the `index` it held in your submitted `devices` array. Bounded by the batch cap, so this is never truncated. Empty until the job completes.

error_message.description: Set only when the job failed.

device_token_masked.description: Masked device credential — the first and last few characters only. The raw token is a sendable credential and is never returned.

sdk_enabled.description: Whether the Arsel SDK is embedded on this device.

contact_id.description: Arsel contact UUID. Mutually exclusive with external_id, email and phone_number.

external_id.description: Your own user id for this contact, the one the mobile and web SDKs identify with. The strongest identifier: tried before email and phone_number, and it survives email and phone changes.

email.description: Contact email. Matched case-insensitively; authoritative when both email and phone_number are supplied.

data_payload.description: Flat string→string map delivered alongside the notification. `arsel_*`, `google*`, `gcm*` and FCM-reserved keys are rejected.

title.description: Notification title. null once the content has been purged.

body.description: Notification body. null once the content has been purged.
body.example: Order A-1023 is on its way.

devices_targeted.description: Devices the contact had registered when the push was sent.

devices_accepted.description: Devices the push provider (FCM, APNs or web push) accepted the notification for. Accepted is not delivered: providers do not confirm arrival on the device.

to.description: Recipient in E.164 format, including the country code.

template_name.description: Name of an APPROVED template in your account. Templates are created and approved before they can be sent.

language.description: Template language code. Omit when your account has exactly one approved template with this name.

parameters.description: Values for the template placeholders, keyed by placeholder name. For an authentication template, pass the one-time code as `code`.

failure_reason.description: Why the send failed. Present only when status is failed.

status.description: Only a `verified` domain can send: any address at it is accepted as `from`.

sender_name.description: The value to pass as `from` when sending SMS.

country.description: The country this sender is approved to send to, as SMS campaigns report it.

purposes.description: What the sender is registered for. Campaigns need `marketing`; messages sent through `POST /v1/sms/send` need `transactional`.

description.example: Spent over 1,000 SAR in the last 90 days

contact_count.description: Contacts matching the segment when it was last counted. `null` while `status` is `processing`.

status.description: `processing` until the members have been computed for the current rules, then `ready`.

filter.description: The rules a contact must match to be in the segment.

limit.description: The plan's limit. `null` means the plan sets no limit.

remaining.description: What is left of `limit`. `null` when there is no limit.

period_end.description: Exclusive: the instant the next period starts.

sms.description: SMS credits. One credit is one message part, so a long message uses several.

contacts.description: Contacts in the organization right now, against the plan limit. Not a per-period counter.

name.description: The domain to send from. Stored lowercased.

required.description: The domain cannot become `verified` until every required record is published. The others are recommended for deliverability.

status.description: Only a `verified` domain can send: any address at it is accepted as `from`.

records.description: The DNS records to publish at the domain's DNS provider.

signature_hash.description: Base64 SHA-256 hash of the app signing key.

otp_type.description: How the recipient gets the code off the screen.

add_security_recommendation.description: Append "For your security, do not share this code." to the body.

code_expiration_minutes.description: Adds a footer reading "This code expires in N minutes."

button_text.description: Button label. Meta supplies a localized default.

autofill_text.description: Label shown while autofilling. One-tap and zero-tap only.

supported_apps.description: Android apps allowed to autofill the code. Required for one-tap and zero-tap.

zero_tap_terms_accepted.description: Must be true for zero-tap: accepts Meta's zero-tap terms.

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: How long Meta may keep retrying delivery before dropping the code.

name.description: Template name: lowercase letters, numbers and underscores, starting with a letter. Unique per language.

components.description: Required for `marketing` and `utility`; not accepted for `authentication`. The template content in Meta's own component format, passed through unchanged: `HEADER` (format `TEXT` only), `BODY`, `FOOTER` and `BUTTONS`. Placeholders are named, in lowercase snake_case: `{{first_name}}`.

authentication.description: Required when `category` is `authentication`. Meta fixes the wording of an authentication template, so you choose options instead of writing components.

name.description: The value to pass as `template_name` when sending.

category.description: Can change after submission: Meta recategorizes templates, and the category sets the price per message.

status.description: Only `approved` templates can be sent. `pending` is under review by Meta; `paused` and `disabled` are applied by Meta for low quality; `draft` means the status is not known yet.

rejection_reason.description: Meta's reason, when the template was rejected.

parameters.description: The keys `POST /whatsapp/send` needs in `parameters` for this template. `["code"]` for an authentication template.

components.description: The template content in Meta's own component format, as stored.

The full replacement content. The template content in Meta's own component format, passed through unchanged: `HEADER` (format `TEXT` only), `BODY`, `FOOTER` and `BUTTONS`. Placeholders are named, in lowercase snake_case: `{{first_name}}`.

description.example: Opened 3+ emails in the last 90 days

filter.description: The rules a contact must match to be in the segment.

description.example: Opened 3+ emails in the last 90 days

filter.description: Replaces the whole rule tree. The members are recomputed, and `status` is `processing` until they are.

enabled.description: Whether Smart Sending was on when the campaign was sent.

skipped.description: Recipients skipped because they had already reached the sending cap.

tracks_revenue.description: Whether this event maps a revenue value.

enabled.description: False when the organization has no conversion events; the other fields are then empty.

tracking_since.description: When the earliest conversion event was enabled.

revenue.description: Attributed revenue, one entry per currency.

failed.description: Messages the mail provider never accepted.

validator_rejected.description: Addresses the email validator rejected before sending. Counted in `bounced`.

delivery_rate.description: `delivered` / `sent`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

open_rate.description: `unique_opens` / `delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

click_rate.description: `unique_clicks` / `delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

bounce_rate.description: `bounced` / `sent`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

unsubscribe_rate.description: `unsubscribed` / `delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

complaint_rate.description: `complained` / `delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

links.description: Clicks per link, most clicked first. Unsubscribe links are left out.

recipients.description: Contacts the campaign was sent to. Before it is sent, the current audience size.

failed.description: Messages the SMS provider never accepted.

unknown.description: Delivery receipts with a status the provider did not name.

pending.description: Accepted by the provider with no final receipt yet.

clicks.description: Every click, repeats included. Link-scanner clicks excluded.

bot_clicks.description: Clicks identified as link scanners. Not counted in `clicks`.

delivery_rate.description: `delivered` / `sent`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

click_rate.description: `unique_clicks` / `delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

recipients.description: Contacts the campaign was sent to. Before it is sent, the contacts it can currently reach.

delivered.description: Notifications accepted by APNs, FCM or Web Push. Acceptance, not arrival on the device.

confirmed.description: Notifications the device reported receiving. A floor: not every device reports.

suppressed.description: Notifications the device received but did not show.

token_invalidations.description: Sends refused because the device token was no longer valid.

bot_opens.description: Opens whose signature failed verification. Not counted in `opens`.

bot_clicks.description: Clicks whose signature failed verification. Not counted in `clicks`.

unique_delivered.description: Contacts with at least one delivered notification.

delivery_rate.description: `delivered` / `attempts`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

open_rate.description: `unique_opens` / `unique_delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

click_rate.description: `unique_clicks` / `unique_delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

expirations.description: Messages that expired on the device without being shown.

bot_impressions.description: Impressions identified as automated. Not counted in `impressions`.

bot_clicks.description: Clicks identified as automated. Not counted in `clicks`.

devices_reached.description: Devices that have shown the message at least once.

click_rate.description: `clicks` / `impressions`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

delivery_rate.description: `delivered` / `sent`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

read_rate.description: `unique_reads` / `delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

click_rate.description: `unique_clicks` / `delivered`. A fraction from 0 to 1. `null` when the denominator is 0.

ContactFilter.description: A group of rules a contact must match. Groups nest up to 10 levels and hold at most 100 rules in total.

from.description: Key of the step it leaves

to.description: Key of the step it enters

type.description: `default` after any step but a condition or a wait. A `condition` leaves by `condition_met` and `condition_not_met`, a `wait_for_event` by `event_received` and `timeout`. A branch with no connection ends the run.

status.description: Enable it as it is created. Refused, and nothing is created, while it has `issues`. Left out, the automation is a `draft`.

steps.description: The whole graph, trigger included. Send it with `connections`; together they replace what was there.

step_key.description: The step it concerns; `null` for the automation as a whole

status.description: `draft` until first enabled; then `enabled` or `disabled`. Only an enabled automation lets contacts in.

steps.description: The latest steps. The trigger is a step too.

issues.description: What must be fixed before the automation can be enabled. Empty when it is ready.

status.description: `draft` until first enabled; then `enabled` or `disabled`. Only an enabled automation lets contacts in.
`enabled` publishes the latest steps and lets contacts in. `disabled` stops new entries; contacts already in finish.

steps.description: The whole graph, trigger included. Send it with `connections`; together they replace what was there. Refused while the automation is enabled, unless this request also sets `status: disabled`.

status.description: `waiting` while the run sits in a delay or a wait; `running` between steps.

current_step_key.description: The step the run is on, or the one it failed on. `null` once it has finished otherwise.

event.description: The trigger event that started the run

event_name.description: For a `custom_event` trigger, the event’s name

outcome.description: The connection the run left by: `default`, or a branch of a `condition` or a `wait_for_event`. `null` when the step failed.

skip_reason.description: Why a message was not sent, e.g. `no_email`, `suppressed`, `smart_sending`

status.description: `waiting` while the run sits in a delay or a wait; `running` between steps.

current_step_key.description: The step the run is on, or the one it failed on. `null` once it has finished otherwise.

steps.description: The steps the run has been through, in order

AutomationTriggerStep.description: What starts a run, and whether a contact may start another. Its target: `contact_created` takes none; `contact_unsubscribed` takes none; `tag_added` needs `tag_id`; `list_added` needs `list_id`; `form_submitted` needs `form_id`; `entered_segment` needs `segment_id`; `email_opened` needs `campaign_id`; `email_clicked` needs `campaign_id`; `email_bounced` needs `campaign_id`; `sms_clicked` needs `campaign_id`; `push_opened` takes `campaign_id` (left out: any); `push_clicked` takes `campaign_id` (left out: any); `in_app_shown` takes `campaign_id` (left out: any); `in_app_clicked` takes `campaign_id` (left out: any); `in_app_dismissed` takes `campaign_id` (left out: any); `custom_event` needs `event_name`. `reentry` unset reads as `always`.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationSendEmailStep.description: Sends from `from_prefix`@`from_domain`, a verified sending domain. `subject` and `preheader` may use merge tags.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationSendSmsStep.description: The sender is chosen per contact from those registered for `purpose` in the contact’s country; `sender_by_country` picks one (country → sender name) where a country has several. `content` may use merge tags.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationSendWhatsappStep.description: `template_name` and `language` name an approved WhatsApp template; `parameters` maps each of its variables to a value, which may use merge tags.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationSendPushStep.description: Sends to every device of the contact. Text may use merge tags.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationShowInAppStep.description: Shows an in-app campaign to the contact.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationAddTagStep.description: Adds the tag to the contact.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationRemoveTagStep.description: Removes the tag from the contact.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationAddToListStep.description: Adds the contact to the list.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationRemoveFromListStep.description: Removes the contact from the list.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationUpdateContactStep.description: Writes the values to the contact as given: merge tags are not rendered. `properties` keys are custom property keys.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationDelayStep.description: Holds the run for `duration`, at most 365 days.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationConditionStep.description: Leaves by `condition_met` when the contact matches `filter`, otherwise by `condition_not_met`.

key.description: Chosen by you and never changed: the step’s identity in connections, runs and results.

AutomationWaitForEventStep.description: Holds the run until the contact’s activity matches `filter` (leaves by `event_received`) or `timeout` passes (leaves by `timeout`).
